HubSpot Company Notes (Aurora Medical Billing)

Overview
- Mid-market medical billing + revenue cycle management vendor (payer/provider workflows).
- Primary interest: batch LLM processing (denial letter summarization, coding assistance, claim note extraction) with strong cost controls.
- They are comparing: (a) Hosted API for fast start vs (b) Dedicated capacity (preferred) for predictable throughput + tighter data controls.

Key contacts (from calls / email)
- Jenna Park — Director, Data Platform (champion).
- Ravi Patel — Lead ML Engineer (owns eval harness).
- Tom Alvarez — InfoSec Manager (questionnaire + evidence pack gatekeeper).
- Maria Nguyen — Procurement (loop-in once deployment model + commercial shape agreed).

What they’re trying to do
- End-of-month processing spikes: ~1.2M claim notes/month with heavy batch windows (last 5 business days).
- Workload shape: mostly batch jobs (async), some internal analyst UX (non-customer facing).
- Current pain: cloud managed endpoints are expensive for sustained batch + unpredictable throttling during peak; they want a predictable throughput plan and a clear $/1k documents model.

Requirements / constraints
- Data: “PHI-adjacent” per Jenna; they believe initial eval dataset can be de-identified but Security has not signed off.
- Compliance posture: they asked specifically for audit logs, retention controls, and KMS integration.
- Access: prefer SSO (SAML) for Console access and least-privilege RBAC for API keys.
- Residency: US-only for any stored logs/metadata.
- Retention: strong preference for minimal/zero retention for request/response payloads; logs must not contain PHI.

Dedicated vs Hosted decision factors (their words)
- Hosted API (pros): fastest for developer onboarding; easiest procurement if low-risk data (de-identified).
- Hosted API (cons): fear of multi-tenant exposure perception + uncertainty on retention/logging details.
- Dedicated (pros): predictable throughput + stronger “comfort” story for InfoSec; easier to communicate controls internally.
- Dedicated (cons): wants commitment to be small enough initially; concerned about paying for idle GPUs outside peak windows.

Evaluation plan (draft, owned by Ravi)
- Duration: 2 weeks once security approves evidence pack access.
- Dataset: 25k–50k de-identified claim notes + denial letters (mix of lengths; they’ll provide distribution).
- Metrics:
  - Cost: target <$0.XX per note equivalent (they track internally as $/1k notes).
  - Throughput: sustain 10–25 req/s batch with 2k–6k token outputs, with predictable job completion time.
  - Quality: extraction accuracy and summarization rubric vs baseline (current provider).
  - Ops: logging/audit requirements met; ability to export audit events to SIEM.
- Output format: prefers structured JSON output for downstream workflow automation.

Recent activity timeline
- 2025-05-16: Inbound intent signal (downloaded regulated workloads page / requested pricing info). Assigned to Diego.
- 2025-05-22: Intro call (Diego + Fatima). Confirmed batch-first use case; cost sensitivity high; asked for Dedicated vs Hosted guidance.
- 2025-05-30: Sent regulated Security FAQ + evidence pack index; Tom requested “what exactly is logged” and “how to configure retention.”
- 2025-06-06: Eval scoping call (Ravi). Agreed on 2-week plan; asked for sample audit log schema + export pattern (pointed to internal example; offered to share redacted sample during security review).
- 2025-06-14: Email thread: they want a one-page Dedicated vs Hosted comparison with focus on data handling + commercial constructs (no surprise overages).
- 2025-06-21: Diego note: Aurora leaning Dedicated if dataset is classified as PHI-adjacent; if Security signs off on de-identified, they might start Hosted for dev and move to Dedicated before production.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Confirm whether Aurora requires a BAA for this workflow or if de-identification is sufficient (route through Naomi Feldman + Michael Grant before committing to any language).
- Provide a simple cost model: expected monthly spend for (a) Hosted batch usage vs (b) Dedicated baseline + burst policy around end-of-month.
- Schedule security questionnaire kickoff; Tom wants evidence pack access under NDA and a point person for fast answers (suggest Olga Petrov).

Internal notes
- Good fit for Optimize story (batching/caching suggestions + predictable economics).
- Buyer motivation is economics + risk reduction, not “best model access.” Keep talk track on throughput predictability, unit cost, and operational controls (audit/export/retention).
- Avoid “HIPAA-ready” phrasing; keep to concrete controls and documented posture.
